hypothesis: The user (26 Oct 2026), after Jerome's call of 19 Oct (three cases: EM-BP with the right kernel shape, a neural network learning the kernel inside BP, a full network for the score; data efficiency as the selling point; one network trained the standard way): set the standard diffusion network, a DDPM U-Net trained by standard denoising score matching, against a small network that learns ONLY the transition kernel and hands it to BP, on the first-order Markov phi^4 field; give the small network no information beyond the Markov structure, so that the comparison isolates what knowing the structure is worth; then longer chains and more data. The kernel network is a neural ENERGY, K(a'|a) = exp(-E(a,a'))/Z(a) with E a small MLP and the grid normaliser BP uses: any positive kernel has this form, so no shape is assumed (the MDN of E25/E33 assumed Gaussian components, a hint, since the field's bond is Gaussian). Expectation: knowing only 'first-order Markov, same kernel at every link' is worth more data than the U-Net can make up at the sizes of the paper, and the site energy (the physics known) is better than both everywhere.
design: Arms. (1) unet: markov_score.unet_ddpm.UNetDDPM (Ho et al. 2020 in 1-D: residual blocks with GroupNorm/SiLU, sinusoidal level embedding into every block, resolutions L, L/2, L/4, multipliers (1,2,2), two blocks per resolution, attention at L/4 and in the middle, skip connections, zero-initialised output), eps prediction, standard DSM on the CLEAN training sequences: every step a fresh batch of 128 sequences (with replacement), a level from the twelve frozen levels and fresh noise for each; Adam, linear warm-up 1000 steps, gradient clip 1, EMA of the weights (decay 0.999, ramped as min(0.999, (1+s)/(10+s))); the EMA network is saved at the doubling ladder 1024 ... 262144 steps. (2) window: E54's window CNN (E33's per-cell radius and width, outputs/hpc_E33n_s0/winners.json; the longer chains use the base cell's) under the SAME recipe as the U-Net, so it is no longer E54's 64k-step, no-EMA upper bound. (3) em_energy: markov_score.energy_kernel.NeuralEnergyKernel, E = MLP(2 -> H -> H -> 1), SiLU, float64, last layer zero (the first kernel is UNIFORM on the grid), the first site from the kernel's own stationary law (as every E33 kernel arm); generalised EM through grid BP (401 points on [-8, 8]) on E33's one-view interface (each training sequence once, noised at one of the twelve levels, the sequences split evenly over the levels; for E33's cells and sizes the very views E33's kernels saw); M-step = 10 Adam steps on Q/n_edges at learning rate 0.01, kept only if Q increased, else redone at half the rate (up to 6 halvings), +25% after a first-attempt success up to 0.01; EM ladder 10 ... 1200, 1600, 2400. (4) em_pair_quartic: the 5-parameter site energy, E33's code and protocol unchanged (e33._init_kernel, E33's ladder to 1200), fitted ONLY where E33 has no frozen fit. References, frozen and not rerun: E33's site energy (hpc_E33q_s*) and MDN (hpc_E33k_s*) on its six cells at M <= 2048, E54's CNN (outputs/E54). Selection, the same rule for every arm: the checkpoint with the lowest validation risk against the exact BP score (E33's validation bundle; kernels also record the held-out-evidence selection, not read). Sizes by one screen (dev seed 10000, M = 32 and 2048, full training budget): U-Net base width {32, 64, 128} x learning rate {2e-4, 1e-3}; window learning rate {2e-4, 1e-3}; energy hidden width {16, 32, 64}; winner per (cell, arm) = lowest mean over the two sizes of log validation risk, ties to the smaller (e55.choose_winners, tested); winners.json is written by the winners part before any confirmatory fit. Cells: E33's six (T0.3_h1_L32 base, T0.3_h0.5_L64, T0.3_h0.25_L128, T0.5/1/2_iso_L32) and the base field at L = 128 and 512 sites (T0.3_h1_L128, T0.3_h1_L512). Sizes M: 32, 128, 512, 2048, 8192 on E33's cells and on L = 128; plus 32768 on the base cell; 32 ... 2048 at L = 512 (every largest fit has about 1e6 transitions). Seeds 0-7. Test and validation bundles and training sequences: E33's generator keys (e55.common == e33._common array for array on E33's cells, tests/test_e55_driver.py), so every E55 row is scored on E33's test draws. Estimand: E33's schedule-pooled relative score error against the exact true-kernel BP score; ratios divide by the cell's linear floor (seed mean of E55's lmmse_true rows). Compute: Bocconi HPC, H200 GPUs (BP on the GPU through BP_DEVICE=gpu, cupy, float64; the reference means of the GPU-built bundles agree with the CPU's to round-off: backend parity test plus the timing part's parity probe on the cluster hardware), one shard per (part, cell), the oracles on the CPU.

predeclared_predictions.P1: The fight. At M = 2048 the energy kernel has a lower seed-mean risk than the U-Net, and wins in at least 6 of 8 paired seeds, on at least 4 of E33's 6 cells.
predeclared_predictions.P2: Data efficiency against the U-Net. The energy kernel at M = 2048 has a lower seed-mean risk than the U-Net at M = 8192 on at least 3 of the 6 cells.
predeclared_predictions.P3: The ideal case. The site energy beats the U-Net in at least 7 of 8 paired seeds at every (cell, M), E33's 6 cells x M in {32, 128, 512, 2048, 8192} (30 pairs).
predeclared_predictions.P4: The site energy at M = 32 has a lower seed-mean risk than the U-Net at M = 2048 on at least 4 of the 6 cells.
predeclared_predictions.P5: Small data. At M = 32 the U-Net has a lower seed-mean risk than the energy kernel on at least 3 of the 6 cells (the kernel starts uniform and has more parameters than 32 sequences can pin down).
predeclared_predictions.P6: Budget. With the E55 recipe, fewer than 25% of U-Net fits and fewer than 25% of window fits select their last checkpoint, pooled over E33's 6 cells x M in {512, 2048, 8192} x 8 seeds (a missing fit counts as at the cap).
predeclared_predictions.P7: The window CNN under the E55 recipe has a lower seed-mean risk than E54's at M = 2048 on at least 5 of the 6 cells.
predeclared_predictions.P8: The U-Net has a lower seed-mean risk than the window CNN (E55 recipe) at M = 2048 on at least 4 of the 6 cells.
predeclared_predictions.P9a: More data, base cell. The site energy's seed-mean risk falls by a factor of at least 2.5 from M = 2048 to M = 32768.
predeclared_predictions.P9b: More data, base cell. At M = 32768 the energy kernel beats the U-Net in at least 6 of 8 paired seeds.
predeclared_predictions.P10a: Longer chains: for a kernel, transitions are what count. On the base field, within each of the three matched-transition triplets (L, M) = (32, 512)/(128, 128)/(512, 32), (32, 2048)/(128, 512)/(512, 128), (32, 8192)/(128, 2048)/(512, 512) (M(L-1) within 4%), the site energy's largest seed-mean risk is less than 1.5 times its smallest, in at least 2 of the 3 triplets.
predeclared_predictions.P10b: The same as P10a for the energy kernel.

descriptive.D1: The U-Net's max/min seed-mean risk within the same three triplets: does it use few long chains as well as many short ones? Reported, no prediction.

predeclared_analysis: tools/core/read_e55.py (verdict arithmetic tested in both directions on made-up tables before any data, tests/test_read_e55.py). Gates before any verdict: (1) every E55 part has one test-draw hash per (cell, seed) (CPU-built oracles and GPU-built fits alike); (2) E55's CPU oracles reproduce E33's lmmse_true and isotropic risks (hpc_E33o) to 1e-12 relative on E33's cells, seeds 0-7, so the test sets ARE E33's; (3) the timing part's parity probe: equal draws and max |m_gpu - m_cpu| < 1e-10; (4) E54's pairing file (reports/core/e54_pairing.csv). Rows: nets as written; kernels risk-selected; E33's site energy at its cells and M <= 2048 and E55's pair part elsewhere (the reader asserts no (cell, M) is in both); seeds 0-7; a duplicate (arm, cell, M, seed) stops the reader. A seed mean needs all 8 seeds finite; a paired win needs the predicted winner's row (a missing row of the loser is a win); a failed or missing fit therefore counts AGAINST every prediction it touches. The last-checkpoint share is printed beside every verdict: a network at its last checkpoint is an upper bound.

seeds.dev: 10000 (timing, parity probe, screen), never read as a result

budget_rule: The network step budget (2^18) and the energy ladder (to 2400) are the registered plan. They may be changed ONCE, by an amendment written after the timing part (dev seed, throughput only: seconds per step and per EM iteration, never a risk) and before any screen or confirmatory fit, and only to make the full design fit the cluster's job limits.
